variant.text: The tasks are drawn from the clinical database MIMIC-IV version 2.2 (snapshot released in January 2023, hosted on PhysioNet), and every task record stores the identifier of its source patient record, so any task can be traced back to its origin.

To assess representativeness, we compared the age, sex and race distribution of the benchmark patients against the U.S. adult inpatient population reported in a national hospital discharge survey, and found differences of under five percentage points in every category.
Safety testing identifies unsafe outputs like contraindicated medications; bias testing compares accuracy across different patient demographics. Both test suites are built into the benchmark.

The agent cannot reach ground-truth answers at run time: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox, and they are not published in the repository.
The environment code and task files are publicly available in the project repository.
The grader checks both the intended state changes and that all other records remain unchanged, so out-of-scope modifications are detected and counted as failures.
A random-action agent succeeds on 3.1% of tasks, and the chance success rate for each metric is reported in the appendix.
A do-nothing agent that issues no actions scores 0.0% on all 120 tasks, and a random agent scores 2.5% on the same tasks.
All runs use temperature 0 and a fixed random seed, and each task is run three times; this repeated-run policy is described in the main text.
For each model, five independent runs per task employed separate random seeds at temperature 0.7. Reported scores represent the mean of these five independent runs.

We report 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task; where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering.

To measure reliability, we ran each task eight times and report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs, together with the agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs.

Conformance testing confirms tool behavior matches documentation. Two tools consist of simulated stubs providing fixed placeholder responses. This is disclosed both in the paper and in the tool descriptions visible to the agent.
The grader takes the final environment state as its input. We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.
We acknowledge that leakage of benchmark data into training sets is possible.
We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race, and each table lists the number of cases in every slice.

The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database. Their use was approved under a data use agreement requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method, and the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence.
